html:
This is the map's label for Japan in 1000, 1100 and 1200, during the Heian period (794 to 1185), when the Fujiwara family dominated the imperial court. The chart's bar is Nara and Heian Japan.

The emperors ruled from Heian-kyō, now Kyoto. The Fujiwara married their daughters to emperors and then governed as regents for their grandsons. Their power peaked under Fujiwara no Michinaga in the early 1000s, who married several daughters to emperors.

It was a court culture of poetry, calligraphy and refined taste. Women writing in the new kana script produced classics: Murasaki Shikibu wrote The Tale of Genji, and Sei Shōnagon wrote The Pillow Book.

From 1086 retired emperors began to rule from behind the throne, weakening the Fujiwara. Real force lay with provincial warrior clans. The Taira and Minamoto fought the Genpei War of 1180 to 1185, and Minamoto no Yoritomo set up the first shogunate at Kamakura, shown on the map as Shogun Japan.
